elements.text:
Credit cards remain structurally relevant across Latin America & the Caribbean, despite rise of alternative payment methods
Credit cards are central to everyday payments across LATAM (~65% cards penetration) and the Caribbean (~$305Bn credit card market volume), with high penetration, strong consumer preference, and a large, growing transaction base.
Cards are a critical driver of client primacy, shaping how customers spend, pay, and engage with their primary bank daily.
Credit cards deliver outsized value and remain a priority growth engine for IB Retail, with solid revenue momentum
Credit cards account for 5% of IB Retail lending balances, yet generate 28% of lending revenue, supported by significantly higher NIMs  vs other lending products (~17%, in F25), positioning cards as a core driver of F26 growth
IB Credit Cards delivered solid F25 revenue growth (+6% Y/Y), driven by NII expansion from lower funding costs, supporting a +108 bps NIM uplift and maintaining a materially higher NIM than CB despite modest fee growth
Monetization however constrained by usage gaps and weak, fragmented loyalty programs
Competitive performance is mixed, with weak acquisition growth vs market but consistently strong usage metrics across countries
Despite low usage (~20% vs 30% benchmark) and high Open-To-Buy (driven by Chile and Mexico), IB continues to deliver solid momentum, with spend and balances up 7% and 8% YoY respectively, alongside improving attrition across key markets
Revolving balances remain stable overall, with Chile under targeted review following TSYS migration accounting adjustments
Fragmentation and limited competitiveness of loyalty programs has led to wide dispersion in cost, engagement and profitability
We are focused on 4 strategic levers to unlock full potential by driving primacy, digital engagement, and profitability across markets 
Grow primacy through credit cards: Deepen existing client relationships through targeted offers, regional and local campaigns, and proactive segment-led retention strategies
Deliver differentiated value proposition: Reinforce card differentiation by relaunching regional, value‑based loyalty program & clearly communicating exclusive, unique benefits
Enable ScotiaMóvil as primary channel: Scale digital onboarding with bundled offerings, elevate ScotiaMóvil self‑service, and accelerate multi‑channel servicing
Strengthen profitability: Convert Mercury benefits into sustained P&L impact, execute authorization uplift initiatives, and drive operational efficiency via product simplification
